Former Synagogue in Hainsfarth

Former Synagogue · Hainsfarth, Germany

The synagogue in Hainsfarth was built in 1860, replacing an earlier prayer house established in 1722 on the same site in what is now Jurastraße. Designed with Neo-Moorish architectural elements, it served the local Jewish community until the Nazi era, when it was vandalized during the November 1938 pogrom. The building later passed into municipal ownership and was used for storage. Restoration beginning in the mid-1980s culminated in its reopening in 1996 as a cultural center and meeting space. The former prayer hall retains its original ceiling and wall paintings, and a plaque commemorates the Jewish residents of Hainsfarth deported and murdered during the Holocaust.
